fields.label: Approved database creation root
fields.help: Optional for registering a server or opening an existing database. Set the approved absolute directory on the Firebird server before creating a database from a server-only connection.

fields.label: Service authentication database context
fields.help: Optional ordinary database path or alias whose server-configured SecurityDatabase and mappings should authenticate Services API requests. Do not enter the security store filename here. This does not change server configuration, the database being opened, or an operation target. Leave empty for the server default; CDEadmin prevents FB_EXPECTED_DB in its process environment from overriding that choice.

fields.label: Network protocol
fields.help: INET tries addresses in application-host resolver order; INET4 restricts resolution to IPv4 and INET6 to IPv6. IPv6 hosts accept ::1 or [::1]; keep the port in its separate field, not inside the host. Scoped addresses use the application host's interface, for example fe80::1%eth0. The server must have an IPv6 listener and a reachable route. Enter the database filename or alias separately. XNET uses local shared memory and requires no TCP port. The application host, not the browser host, must run Windows. Firebird 5 does not support WNET named pipes. Unsupported selections are rejected, never replaced with TCP.

fields.label: Authentication plugin preference list
fields.help: Ordered native AuthClient list for database creation, attachment and Services API. Separate case-sensitive plugin names with commas, spaces, tabs or semicolons. Native negotiation selects a compatible installed plugin; this does not install plugins or change AuthServer. An unavailable-only or nonmatching list fails; CDEadmin never retries with a broader list. Legacy_Auth cannot satisfy Required wire encryption. Win_Sspi requires Windows. Do not leave an explicit list empty.

fields.label: Use trusted authentication
fields.help: Windows Win_Sspi authentication requires the CDEadmin application host (not merely the browser or database server) to run Windows. Linux and macOS reject this selection without password fallback. Windows native login qualification is separate from authentication mapping DDL.

fields.label: Save default connection credentials
fields.help: Store the credentials for the default user in CDEadmin. Credentials entered while connecting as another user are never stored as the default credentials.

fields.label: SQL authorization identity
fields.help: Embedded mode uses filesystem authorization, not password authentication. SQL privileges still apply to this identity.

fields.label: Wire encryption policy
fields.help: Required refuses an unencrypted connection. Enabled permits native negotiation, including plaintext when allowed by both sides. Disabled cannot connect to a server requiring encryption. This protects network traffic, not database files. No automatic policy downgrade is attempted.

fields.label: Wire encryption plugin preference list
fields.help: Optional ordered native WireCryptPlugin list, for example ChaCha64,ChaCha. Separate case-sensitive names with commas, spaces, tabs or semicolons. Uses installed client/server plugins; does not install them. Omit for native defaults. Arc4 is a legacy compatibility choice, not the preferred default. Required needs a compatible encryption plugin and authentication key. Windows/macOS native qualification is separate.

fields.label: Enable wire compression
fields.help: Client preference for native network compression (protocol 13 or later); the server follows the negotiated request. Can be combined with wire encryption, but does not encrypt traffic itself. Disabled by default. Applies to new connections, not existing sessions. Database MON$WIRE_COMPRESSED reports the negotiated state; enabling this option alone is not proof of compression. Do not also set WireCompression in additional native configuration. Windows/macOS require separate native runtime qualification.

fields.label: Per-connection wire encryption configuration
fields.help: Audited native client text: WireCrypt, WireCryptPlugin, WireCompression, AuthClient, ConnectionTimeout, DummyPacketInterval, TcpNoNagle and ClientBatchBuffer. One key=value per line; comments and quoted values are supported. Maximum 16 KiB UTF-8. Includes, macros, blocks, duplicate or unknown keys and server/engine settings are rejected. Do not repeat a dedicated wire, dummy or authentication field. Exception: explicit connection timeout uses native DPB/SPB precedence over raw ConnectionTimeout. Blank removes this override; unrelated Python driver defaults are not inherited. This does not edit firebird.conf or install plugins. Windows/macOS native qualification is separate.

fields.label: Initial DECFLOAT trap policy
fields.help: Custom requires at least one trap: an empty attachment list means native defaults, not disable all traps. Applies to new attachments including creation and is restored by ALTER SESSION RESET. Not a stored database setting.

fields.label: Initial DECFLOAT rounding mode
fields.help: Native default sends no rounding override. Applies to this attachment, including after ALTER SESSION RESET. It does not alter stored database values.

fields.label: Attachment linger policy
fields.help: Applies on the next existing-database attachment. Suppress clears the current shared SuperServer cache's linger timer, not the stored LINGER setting. No effect in SuperClassic or Classic. Native default sends no override and does not restore a timer already suppressed.

fields.label: Attachment page-cache policy
fields.help: Native default sends no attachment override. This preference applies to new attachments, including database creation, and does not change existing sessions or stored database buffers.

fields.label: Requested attachment cache pages
fields.help: This request does not change stored database buffers. SuperServer ignores it. SuperClassic/Classic use a minimum allocation of 50 pages, and stored nonzero buffers take precedence. Server architecture and available memory can reduce allocation. Read actual allocation in database properties.

fields.label: Initial parallel-worker policy
fields.help: Native default uses the server's ParallelWorkers configuration. Applies to new attachments, including creation, and survives ALTER SESSION RESET. Existing sessions and stored database settings are unchanged.

fields.label: Requested parallel workers
fields.help: Zero is an explicit zero request, not the native default. Positive requests are capped by the server's MaxParallelWorkers configuration. This is an attachment preference, not a count of workers executing a task or a backup/restore service setting.

fields.label: Disable cooperative garbage collection
fields.help: Applies when attaching to an existing database. Firebird 5.0 does not apply this flag to the initial database-creation attachment.

fields.label: Native autocommit (writes cannot be rolled back later)
No auto undo (native rollback still applies)
Session idle timeout (seconds; 0 uses database policy)
Connection timeout (seconds)
fields.help: Native connection-establishment wait for database attachment, creation and Services. Blank uses native configuration; zero makes the protocol-establishment read wait immediate, not unlimited. DNS resolution and operating-system TCP connection attempts can take longer; this is not a total wall-clock deadline, statement timeout or idle-session timeout. Windows/macOS require separate native timing qualification.

fields.label: Dummy packet interval (seconds)
fields.help: Native DummyPacketInterval configuration for new database and Services connections. Blank uses native configuration; zero disables dummy packets. A positive interval can send native dummy packets while waiting for network input. It is not a background heartbeat for an idle application, a disconnect deadline or an OS TCP-keepalive setting. Do not also set DummyPacketInterval in additional native configuration. Windows/macOS require separate native traffic qualification.

fields.label: Approved local database directory
fields.help: Directory on the application host, not the browser. Local file access grants embedded access; a password is not checked.
